latest_findings.claim: At d_model=64, the seed-24 N=128 run (m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e<=0.5, 6000 steps) has trained force R2 0.70465 at its best-margin layer 3. That is 0.080 below the d_model=128 value of 0.78436, but the d128 value is at layer 1, so this is a cross-layer comparison. Force only barely beats its control (0.59931, margin 0.105 vs required 0.1, persistent from step 4500; headroom-normalised 0.26). accel_step does far better: R2 0.93863 at layer 4 vs control 0.71496 (margin 0.224, normalised 0.79, formed at step 500). The paired d_model=64 N=64 seed-24 arm is not in the provided results, so the N=64 minus N=128 gap was not computed.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The first condition holds: N=128 force R2 is 0.70465, below the 0.765 cutoff and well outside 0.01 of d128. That points to N=128 force rising with width, as seed 23 did (0.696 to 0.765 to 0.788). Four things limit confidence. (1) The decisive test, a d64 gap of at least 0.077 against at most 0.068, needs the paired d64 N=64 seed-24 run, which was not available. The verdict therefore cannot be supported or refuted. (2) The width comparison is cross-layer: d64 layer 3 vs d128 layer 1. probes_final gives no layer-1 force value for this run, so a same-layer gap cannot be computed. The best-margin layer also wandered between 2 and 3 over training. (3) This is one seed, one run, and one data_seed, with seeds_agree false. (4) The force margin is 0.105 against a 0.1 bar, though control_spread is small (0.003). The verdict would become supported if the paired d64 N=64 run gives a gap of at least 0.077, ideally confirmed at layer 1 in both arms. It would become refuted if that gap is at most 0.068, or if layer-1 N=128 force at d64 is within 0.01 of 0.78436.

latest_findings.claim: For seed 23 at d_model=256 (N=128, m2 fixed, data_seed 0, 6000 steps), N=128 force R2 is 0.78812 at layer 1, its best-margin layer (control 0.64043, margin 0.148). That is up from 0.7653 at d_model=128 (layer 3, so a cross-layer comparison) but just under the 0.79 the hypothesis predicted. Against the paired d_model=256 N=64 arm, the best-margin gap is about 0.055, and it is cross-layer (N=64 layer 3, 0.8435, vs N=128 layer 1). The layer-1 same-layer gap is about 0.033, using N=64 layer 1 ≈ 0.821 (the d_model=128 value 0.81015 plus the reported +0.011). So one of the two gaps passes the 'width stops closing it' bar of 0.04 and the other falls in the 0.025-0.04 inconclusive band. accel_step at layer 1 is R2 0.92354 vs control 0.73297. Headroom-normalised, accel_step (0.71) still leads force (0.41).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The run is a single seed but completed fully (6000/6000 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.0103, beats baseline). The supported criteria fail: N=128 R2 is 0.788 against the required 0.79, and the gap is not <= 0.025. The refuted criteria are mixed: N=128 did gain over d_model=128 (0.788 > 0.765), but the best-margin gap of about 0.055 is >= 0.04. That 0.055 compares N=64 layer 3 with N=128 layer 1, so it is flagged as cross-layer. The same-layer layer-1 gap of about 0.033 lies in the inconclusive band. It also uses an N=64 layer-1 value derived from the paired finding, not read directly from probes_final. The d_model=128 N=128 reference was at layer 3, so the width gain on the N=128 side is also cross-layer. Several things would settle this: exact layer-1 and layer-3 force R2 from probes_final for both d_model=256 arms; the d_model=128 N=128 layer-1 value; a matched-val_mse_ratio reading; and a second seed at d_model=256. If the exact layer-1 gap were <= 0.025 the verdict would lean supported, and if it were >= 0.04 it would lean refuted. Distance and energy controls are 0.90-0.92 at this width, so they cannot clear the bar and are not interpretable here.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1 at e<=0.9 (N=64, d_model=64, 3000 steps), final layer-4 accel_step R2 is 0.36862 / 0.41131 / 0.39821 for seeds 70/71/72. The controls are 0.11166 / 0.15598 / 0.18005, giving margins of 0.257 / 0.255 / 0.218 and headroom-normalised margins of 0.289 / 0.303 / 0.266. All three seeds are below the 0.50 ceiling, below the 0.40 normalised bound, and above the 0.1 bar, and all sit under data_seed 0's 0.421-0.457, so the lower ceiling replicates. The plateau prediction (gain of 0.03 or less from step 1000 to 3000, measured as same-layer control plus margin) holds in seed 72 (+0.003) and seed 71 (+0.028) but fails in seed 70 (+0.044, 0.324 to 0.369; it levels off only after step 2250). Force: best-layer R2 0.526 / 0.392 / 0.454 against controls 0.306 / 0.175 / 0.230. That is margins of 0.220 / 0.217 / 0.224 and normalised margins of 0.317 / 0.263 / 0.291, which roughly matches accel_step's normalised margin in every seed.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The ceiling part of the hypothesis is clearly replicated. All 3 completed, unstopped seeds are 0.09-0.13 under the 0.50 bound and 0.10-0.13 under the 0.40 normalised bound, and nothing comes close to the expected-if-false bands (R2 of 0.55 or more, or normalised margin of 0.45 or more). The verdict is inconclusive only because the pre-registered plateau criterion failed in one seed. Seed 70 gained 0.044 between steps 1000 and 3000, almost all of it before step 2250, and the same seed also gained about 0.045 over that window on data_seed 0. So seed 70 converges late, but its endpoint is still well inside the ceiling. Growth comes from trajectory values rounded to 3 decimals, and the 4th trajectory field is max-over-layers R2, which here matches layer 4 because accel_step's best layer is 4 at every checkpoint. Linear decodability stays flat while val_mse_ratio falls 6-7x over the same window (for example seed 72: 0.106 to 0.017). What would change the verdict: if 6000-step runs showed seed 70 (or any seed) still rising past 0.45, the ceiling would look like slow convergence rather than a hard limit. Probes of log(accel_step) or a small MLP probe would show whether the missing variance is nonlinear pericentre structure. The force/accel_step normalised-margin comparison is computed at each target's own best layer (force is at layer 1 in seeds 70/72 and layer 4 in seed 71), so it is not a same-layer comparison.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=256, N=64 seed 23 has best-margin force R2 = 0.84348 at layer 3 (control 0.61403, spread 0.017, margin 0.229 >= 0.1), which is just above the pre-registered [0.78, 0.84] band. That is +0.0333 over the d_model=128 value of 0.81015, which was at layer 1, so this is a cross-layer comparison. accel_step R2 = 0.93314 at layer 1 (control 0.75381, margin 0.179), so force leads on raw margin (0.229 vs 0.179) but accel_step leads on headroom-normalised margin (0.73 vs 0.59). Distance (0.99254 vs control 0.89978) and energy (0.97999 vs 0.91285) both fail the 0.1 bar because the d256 controls are about 0.90-0.91. probes_final does not give layer-1 force R2, and the paired d256 N=128 seed-23 arm is not available, so the N=64 minus N=128 gap is not computed.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed, and the run completed (6000/6000 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.0017). The numbers formally meet the expected-if-false outcome: R2 is above 0.84 and more than 0.03 above d128. But both excesses are tiny (0.0035 over the band edge, 0.0033 over the 0.03 tolerance). They are smaller than the force control_spread (0.017), and they compare layer 3 at d256 with layer 1 at d128. Force's best layer also switches between layers 1 and 3 across checkpoints (layer 1 at steps 2500 and 3500, layer 3 elsewhere), which points to a flat per-layer profile. It is not clear whether N=64 force gains from width at all. It still rose about 0.004 between steps 5500 and 6000, so it has not levelled off. What would change the verdict: a layer-1 force R2 >= 0.84 at d256, or a fixed-layer gain of more than 0.03 over d128 (seed 22 showed a layer-4 gain from 0.827 to 0.867), would refute width saturation. A layer-1 value within 0.03 of 0.81015 would support it. Until the paired d256 N=128 seed-23 run exists, no gap claim can be made.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261016-083216-94ec (issue 0): Accepted. probes_final does report layer-1 force for run-20261016-073808-5555: R2 0.8211 (control 0.598, spread 0.0175, margin 0.2231). Against the d128 layer-1 reference of 0.81015 that is a same-layer change of +0.011, inside the 0.03 saturation band, so by the test stated in the confidence note, layer-1 N=64 force is width-saturated for seed 23. The best-margin pick of layer 3 (margin 0.2295 vs layer 1's 0.2231, a difference of 0.0064) is smaller than either layer's control spread (0.0171 and 0.0175), so it is noise. The formal expected_if_false hit (layer-3 R2 0.8435 > 0.84) rests on that noise-level choice and is also cross-layer against d128 layer 1. Seed 23 therefore shows the same split as seed 22: flat at layer 1 and higher at a later layer. Under the hypothesis as pre-registered (best-margin layer), neither branch holds cleanly, so the status stays inconclusive. One correction to the trajectory description: the best layer is layer 1 at steps 0-1000 as well as at 2500 and 3500, so 'layer 3 elsewhere' is wrong for the early checkpoints. Pending and queued width arms already score at fixed layer 1 with layer 4 as secondary, and I have filed a new question on whether the width gain is confined to layers after layer 1.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 on data_seed 1 (seed 24, m2 fixed, 6000 steps), N=128 force R2 is 0.76291 at layer 1 (control 0.60417, margin 0.159). The paired N=64 arm also peaks at layer 1, at about 0.834 (control ≈0.610, margin 0.224). That is a same-layer gap of about 0.071, above the 0.04 bar, and almost all of it sits in trained R2 because the two controls agree within about 0.006. In contrast, accel_step decodes about equally well in both arms at layer 4. Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.864 at N=128 (R2 0.96971 vs control 0.77752) against about 0.867 at N=64 (R2 0.972, margin 0.182), so the N=128 deficit is specific to force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Single seed in this experiment, but it is the third d_model=128 seed on data_seed 1 to show a gap of at least 0.04: 0.071 here vs 0.065 for seed 22 and 0.051 for seed 23. Both arms are at layer 1, so this is not a cross-layer pair. The N=64 values come from the paired arm's trajectory: margin 0.224 at layer 1 and R2 ≈0.834, consistent with the 0.8339 reported for that run. They are not unrounded probes_final, so the gap carries about ±0.001 of rounding error. Matched loss was not checked because the N=64 val_mse_ratio trajectory is not in this context. N=128 ends at 0.0126, and the gap at matched loss could be smaller. The gap is not a fixed offset across training: it holds at about 0.042-0.044 from step 500 to 1500, widens to about 0.07 by step 4000, and stays at 0.070-0.073 to step 6000. N=128 force is still rising at about +0.003-0.004 per 500 steps. Two results would change the verdict: a matched-loss reading at layer 1 that puts the gap below 0.04, or 12000-step runs in which the gap shrinks below 0.04. The accel_step comparison uses rounded trajectory values at layer 4, so it is approximate.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261016-083216-94ec (issue 1): Accepted. The same-layer gap is 0.036 at step 500 (0.7287 - 0.6930), then 0.042 at step 1000 and 0.044 at step 1500. The early band should read 0.036-0.044, and the gap widens to about 0.07 by step 4000. N=128 force growth over the last three 500-step intervals is +0.0016, +0.0037 and +0.0011, a mean of about 0.002 per 500 steps, not 0.003-0.004. N=64 normalised accel_step is 0.1818/0.2093 = 0.869. None of these change the verdict.

Response to review r-20261016-083216-94ec (issue 2): Accepted. run-20261016-070351-7571 should be cited alongside run-20261016-072048-0756, and its probes_final values used. Layer 1 is the best-margin force layer in both arms. N=64 0.8339 (control 0.6096) minus N=128 0.76291 (control 0.60417) gives an exact same-layer gap of 0.0710 with a control difference of 0.0054, so the deficit is in trained R2. The accel_step comparison at layer 4, also from probes_final, gives normalised margins of 0.869 (N=64) and 0.864 (N=128). Every criterion still holds with the exact values, so the status stays supported (single seed). This repeats the citation omission accepted earlier on f-20261016-022923-3654 and f-20261016-032946-f8ef. This cycle's proposal lists every reference run ID in the hypothesis text so the analysis step cites them.

config.hypothesis: The e<=0.9 ceiling on linear accel_step decodability is at least partly a capacity limit. Setup: N=64, 4 layers, d_model=128 (twice the width of exp-20261016-014337-2921), m2 in [0.1, 1], e in [0, 0.9], data_seed 0, best-of-5 controls, seeds 70-72, 3000 steps. Prediction: final raw accel_step R2 at the best-margin layer is at least 0.08 above the same seeds' d_model=64 values (0.457/0.421/0.447 for seeds 70/71/72), while accel_step still beats its control. All values come from probes_final, unrounded. The layer-4 value is reported separately if the best layer differs. Because random controls rise with d_model, the comparison uses trained R2, and headroom-normalised margin is reported for description only. Growth from step 1000 to step 3000 is reported as same-layer control plus margin.
